Privacy and Network Access Policy
vlc-privacy
<p>In order to protect your privacy, <i>VLC media player</i> does <b>not</b> collect personal data or transmit them, not even in anonymized form, to anyone.</p>
<p>Nevertheless, <i>VLC</i> is able to automatically retrieve information about the media in your playlist from third party Internet-based services. This includes cover art, track names, artist names and other meta-data.</p>
<p>Consequently, this may entail identifying some of your media files to third party entities. Therefore the <i>VLC</i> developers require your express consent for the media player to access the Internet automatically.</p>

nMain interfaces settings
Main interfaces
Settings for the main interface
Control interfaces
Settings for VLC's control interfaces
Hotkeys settings
Audio
Audio settings
General audio settings
Output modules
General settings for audio output modules.
Filters
Audio filters are used to process the audio stream.
Audio resampler
Visualizations
Audio visualizations
Miscellaneous
Miscellaneous audio settings and modules.
Video
Video settings
General video settings
General settings for video output modules.
Video filters are used to process the video stream.
Subtitles / OSD
Settings related to On-Screen-Display, subtitles and "overlay subpictures"
Splitters
Video splitters separate the stream into multiple videos.
Input / Codecs
Settings for input, demultiplexing, decoding and encoding
Access modules
Settings related to the various access methods. Common settings you may want to alter are HTTP proxy or caching settings.
Demuxers
Demuxers are used to separate audio and video streams.
Video codecs
Settings for the video, images or video+audio decoders and encoders.
Audio codecs
Settings for the audio-only decoders and encoders.
Subtitle codecs
Settings for subtitle, teletext and CC decoders and encoders.
Stream filters
Stream filters are special modules that allow advanced operations on the input side of VLC. Use with care...
Stream output
Stream output settings are used when acting as a streaming server or when saving incoming streams.
Streams are first muxed and then sent through an "access output" module that can either save the stream to a file, or stream it (UDP, HTTP, RTP/RTSP).
Sout streams modules allow advanced stream processing (transcoding, duplicating...).
General stream output settings
Sout stream
Sout stream modules allow to build a sout processing chain. Please refer to the Streaming Howto for more information. You can configure default options for each sout stream module here.
Muxers
Muxers create the encapsulation formats that are used to put all the elementary streams (video, audio, ...) together. This setting allows you to always force a specific muxer. You should probably not do that.
You can also set default parameters for each muxer.
Access output
Access output modules control the ways the muxed streams are sent. This setting allows you to always force a specific access output method. You should probably not do that.
You can also set default parameters for each access output.
Packetizers
Packetizers are used to "preprocess" the elementary streams before muxing. This setting allows you to always force a packetizer. You should probably not do that.
You can also set default parameters for each packetizer.
VLC's implementation of Video On Demand
Playlist
Settings related to playlist behaviour (e.g. playback mode) and to modules that automatically add items to the playlist ("service discovery" modules).
General playlist behaviour
Services discovery
Services discovery modules are facilities that automatically add items to playlist.
Advanced
Advanced settings. Use with care...
